vignette: Jonathan is a 29-year-old European male who serves as a member of the local coast guard. He has been in a committed relationship for over two years and describes his partner, Sarah, as his rock through challenging times. Jonathan first sought therapy after experiencing intense anxiety and flashbacks following an unexpected mugging while he was walking home late one night. On that fateful evening, Jonathan had just finished a long shift at the coast guard station and decided to walk home to clear his mind before resting. As he walked down a dimly lit street, a man suddenly approached him from behind, demanded his wallet, and threatened him with a knife. Despite staying calm and complying with the assailant’s demands, Jonathan was violently pushed to the ground as the attacker fled the scene. Since then, Jonathan has experienced recurrent nightmares where he relives the mugging in vivid detail. During these dreams, he wakes up drenched in sweat and trembling with fear, often unable to fall back asleep until Sarah comforts him in bed. This has disrupted his sleep significantly, leading to increased irritability during the day and a general sense of exhaustion. At work, Jonathan struggles to focus on his duties as a member of the coast guard. His attention is often preoccupied by intrusive thoughts about the mugging, which makes it difficult for him to concentrate during training exercises or when conducting routine patrols. He has also become hypervigilant, constantly scanning his surroundings for any signs of danger. This hyperawareness sometimes manifests as sudden jolts and startle responses at unexpected noises, causing momentary lapses in judgment. Jonathan’s relationships have been strained by the trauma. At work, he finds himself increasingly isolated from his colleagues because he avoids social interactions and tends to keep to himself. He fears that sharing his feelings might make him appear vulnerable or weak. Even with Sarah, Jonathan has become emotionally distant, withdrawing into a shell of silence rather than discussing what happened during the mugging. Despite these challenges, Jonathan is determined not to let the trauma define him. On weekends, he tries to maintain some semblance of normalcy by going on boat rides with Sarah and their friends, an activity he once loved. However, even in these seemingly safe environments, he sometimes feels a wave of panic rise within him when someone approaches too quickly or touches his shoulder unexpectedly. Jonathan often reflects on the incident, wondering if there was anything he could have done differently to prevent it from happening. These thoughts are compounded by feelings of guilt and shame for not being able to protect himself more effectively. He has also started avoiding certain areas in town that remind him of the mugging, limiting his daily activities and social outings. Recently, Jonathan’s supervisor at the coast guard station noticed a decline in his performance and suggested he seek help from a mental health professional. While initially resistant due to concerns about appearing weak or unfit for duty, Jonathan decided to take this step after Sarah reassured him that seeking support would not diminish his strength but rather empower him to overcome his challenges. Jonathan’s journey through therapy has been slow but steady. He acknowledges the ongoing struggle with PTSD symptoms and is committed to working on coping strategies that can help him regain a sense of control over his life without feeling overwhelmed by past trauma.
